title: KIISU V4BR Review: A Card-Sized Flipper Zero cheaper Alternative
content_md: The Flipper Zero made portable hardware experimentation accessible to a much wider audience. The KIISU V4BR board takes a different approach to the same idea: keep the familiar Flipper ecosystem, but place it on a thin, credit-card-sized development board. In this article, I will explain what KIISU is, examine its hardware and supported functions, compare it with Flipper Zero, and discuss several issue I encountered during testing. SAPSAN provided the KIISU V4BR used for this review. The observations and opinions in this article are my own. What is KIISU? KIISU V4BR is open-source development board designed by RainWalker. Its purpose is to provide many of the functions – if not all – seen with Flipper Zero in a credit card style format.
